text:
alex: quick RFC follow-up. i pushed a minimal sketch for a lease-window prefetch model that lives in transport adapters. want short takes before i update the doc.

maria: short answer: keep public APIs stable if possible. we shouldn't force users to learn new call args.

alex: agreed. public iterables unchanged. transports opt-in by advertising a session lease window and a capability set. sdk/coordinator manages leases.

jeff: pls be explicit about duplicates and monotonic fallback. if grpc returns a page early and http later also returns it, we must dedupe reliably.

sam: we dedupe by resume token + lineage epoch + checksum. adapter returns the token; coordinator maintains a seen set per-session and drops duplicates.

natalie: curious about billing: prefetch reservations could surprise hosted customers if we bill them immediately. what's the plan?

alex: reservation model = soft lease. metric reserved_slots increments when prefetch pulled into cache. billing occurs only when page is materialized to the consumer. eviction => no charge. we'll document in console and make defaults conservative.

maria: what about backpressure? adapter prefetch shouldn't outpace consumer and OOM or waste buffers.

alex: coordinator grants lease tokens per-session (token-bucket style). prefetch consumes tokens; tokens are returned as consumer advances. if tokens are exhausted, prefetch stalls. language-agnostic.

jeff: go semantics: be explicit. Pages(ctx, req...) must cancel prefetch on ctx.Done(). background retries must respect context.

sam: retries: keep single logical RetryConfig on the call. Prefetch follows it but adapters may apply a lower cap (e.g., 5 attempts) and more conservative backoff to avoid aggressive cross-transport fanout. prefetch failures are soft: they don't block the current page; unresolved prefetch results in an error when consumer pulls that page.

natalie: operator signals: we need metrics and admin traces: reserved_slots, active_leases, prefetch_failures, dedup_drops, lineage_epoch per-session. add an admin endpoint that lists active leases for a tenant.

alex: also proposing a flag rename: disable_client_prefetch (default false). for customers needing server-side strictness, set to true -> no client prefetch/reservations.

maria: good. any change to retry semantics visible to users? they should still reason in terms of the logical call-level retry.

alex: yes: from user POV one RetryConfig controls on-demand and prefetch retries. adapters can choose transport-local caps but must not violate logical policy. i'll add a short example in py/ts/go showing unchanged pages() signatures and transport opt-ins.

jeff: last ops ask: ensure resume token spec includes stable page id + epoch + checksum; document how servers bump epoch when cursors are reparented.

sam: ok. action items for RFC edit: 1) public surface unchanged, 2) transport capability handshake + lease-window sketch, 3) soft reservation vs bill semantics, 4) resume token spec + dedupe rules, 5) metrics + admin trace, 6) disable_client_prefetch flag + deployment defaults, 7) context cancellation semantics for go.

alex: thanks all. i'll update the RFC and drop a 30m sync invite. :thumbsup:
